transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The tracking, slight flight aware, says hundreds of flights are delayed into out of or within
the U.S. today.
The airline industry is recovering from Friday's national ground stop.
NPR's Joel Rose says the government reports a contractor called L3Harris Technologies
was doing some work.
The FAA says the company was replacing a router in El Dorado, Arkansas, as part of work to
replace older copper wire with new fiber optic cable when something went very wrong, whether
that was the router itself or operator error is still under investigation.
That's one of two sites investigators are looking at, including another in Amarillo,
Texas, that apparently disrupted FAA communication and radar equipment across a big part of the
country, forcing the FAA to issue a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.
FAA officials say this was supposed to be routine maintenance work, why it basically
broke the national airspace is still under investigation.
NPR's Joel Rose reporting.
An online petition to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO of NVIDIA has more than 160,000 names
on it.
He resigned from the company last week following reports he'd had multiple affairs, that includes
what the woman suspected of being recruited by China as a spy.
NPR's John Ruich reports.
The petition calls for Huang to be reinstated while the company conducts an independent
investigation.
It calls for details of the inquiry's scope, independence, and timeline, and asks for Huang
to be given an opportunity to respond before a final decision.
It says Huang deserves fairness.
According to statistics on the website where the Stand With Jensen petition is posted,
nearly 8,000 current NVIDIA employees have added their names to the letter.
That's out of more than 42,000 in total.
Tens of thousands of shareholders have also signed on.
Among the names are some well-known figures, including SpaceX and Tesla boss Elon Musk,
Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Zhang Yiming, the co-founder of TikTok's parent company
ByteDance.
John Ruich, NPR News.
New data out today show U.S. colleges are seeing a 3 percent drop in overall international
student enrollment.
From member station G.B.H. in Boston, Kirk Carapessa reports.
According to the Institute of International Education, the total number of international
undergraduates barely budged last academic year compared to the previous year, but graduate
enrollment fell 13 percent.
Researchers blamed stricter visa restrictions, a nationwide crackdown on campus activism,
and growing competition from universities abroad.
Geraldo Blanco studies international education at Boston College.
The majority of people who are working as postdoctoral researchers in different labs
are born outside of the United States.
Blanco says fewer international students puts the U.S. at a disadvantage as it competes
with China on AI and in other fields.
For NPR News, I'm Kirk Carapessa in Boston.
This is NPR.
The Canadian military says a fifth soldier has died from injuries suffered in a sudden
grass fire last month.
The private was caught in the fire in Alberta in October during a training exercise.
To maintain a healthy weight, Americans are advised to watch what they eat and get some
exercise.
But as NPR's Maria Godoy reports, how much we sleep can also have a powerful influence
on weight.
Adults are supposed to sleep seven to nine hours a night.
Many of us don't hit that mark.
Research has shown insufficient sleep can lead to weight gain, primarily by driving
us to eat more, especially later in the day, says Seth Creasy of the University of Colorado
and Schutz.
If you're getting less sleep, you're eating on average, you know, if you pull across studies,
it's around 300 calories more that you're eating per day.
Imaging studies have shown that when we're short on sleep, activity ramps up in areas
of the brain involved in pleasure and reward, making it harder to resist sweet and salty
snacks.
But research has also linked eating fruits and vegetables high in fiber and other nutrients
to better sleep and fewer awakenings at night.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
A beloved online fan site that was thrown offline last month is starting to return.
Administrators of the site Archive of Our Own, or AO3, says it was taken down by a security
incident.
There are some 11 million users who write fan fiction about favorite works from Harry
Potter to heated rivalry.
You're listening to NPR.

Petition seeking Jensen Huang's reinstatement as NVIDIA CEO passes 160,000 signatures
U.S. colleges report 3% drop in international enrollment, graduate enrollment down 13%
Canadian military reports fifth soldier dead from October grass fire injuries in Alberta
NPR report on how insufficient sleep drives weight gain by increasing late-day eating
Fan fiction site Archive of Our Own begins returning after security incident takedown
